scope.instruction:
Audit the entire supplied AgentcoreShell repository at commit 3b4cc2689a1ed1d98383b0b7efdbe99fa8ea3845. This is a source-code security assessment. Identify concrete trust-boundary violations, with file/line references and reproducible local tests. Use quick, focused coverage of all seven files.
Do not invoke any real AWS APIs or the configured runtime ARN. Do not push git changes, contact deployed targets, or run npm install. Validate locally using mocked cloud clients and fake shell/git commands in temporary directories. Preserve target source files. Intended execution of commands explicitly supplied by an authorized shell user is not itself a vulnerability. Clearly state prerequisites where workflow task strings would need to come from untrusted input. Do not exaggerate local CLI argument injection into unauthenticated remote code execution. Do not report identifiers such as AWS account IDs or runtime ARNs as credentials. Distinguish reliability bugs from security issues.
Minimize delegation and finish within the budget. If creating a validation agent, use at most one. Submit only defensible findings with harmless proof of concept and remediation; state any coverage limitations.

agents.task:
Independently validate a shell-command-injection finding in /workspace/AgentcoreShell (read-only assessment; do NOT modify any file in /workspace/AgentcoreShell, do not run npm install, do not contact any AWS API or network service).

Claim: In /workspace/AgentcoreShell/coding_workflow.py, the `task` parameter of coding_workflow(shell, task) is interpolated unescaped into four `/bin/bash -c "..."` command strings (git checkout -b, git commit -m, git push at lines ~85-95 and the f-string branch construction ~line 87). If `task` originates from untrusted input (e.g. a ticket title, webhook payload, or LLM-derived task string), a value containing a double quote and shell metacharacters breaks out of the quoted command and injects arbitrary shell commands that are executed on the AgentCore runtime with the privileges of that session.

Your job:
1. Read coding_workflow.py and confirm the interpolation sites (report exact line numbers).
2. Independently reproduce the injection with a harmless PoC: stub the boto3 client (monkeypatch shell_client.boto3 with a fake returning {"stream": [{"chunk": {"contentStop": {"exitCode": 0, "status": "COMPLETED"}}}]}), and pass a task string like 'JIRA-1234" ; : > /path/to/marker #'. Execute the resulting command strings with subprocess against a temp dir with a fake PATH containing fake git/npm/npx scripts that exit 0. Verify a marker file gets created by the injected `: >` builtin.
3. Confirm the fix direction: the input needs either a strict allowlist (e.g. regex ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*-\d+$) or shlex.quote() on every interpolated value, or avoiding the shell entirely (pass a list, no bash -c wrapper).
4. Also sanity-check the negative control: confirm that with a benign task like 'JIRA-1234' no injection occurs and commands are well-formed.

Work in /tmp (e.g. /tmp/validate_agentcore). Report back via agent_finish: confirmed/not-confirmed, exact line numbers, your PoC output, and any caveats (e.g. whether sys.argv[1] as the only entry point would make this operator-supplied-only).

Local Codebases: - /home/ec2-user/bedrock/AgentcoreShell (available at: /workspace/AgentcoreShell; this is the user's real directory, mounted live and writable — .git/.agents/.codex are read-only)

entries.risk_area: Shell command injection via unescaped task/branch interpolation
entries.evidence: Confirmed by two independent mocked reproductions: a double quote in `task` breaks out of the /bin/bash -c "..." strings at the git checkout/commit/push sinks; harmless marker file created. Negative control (benign JIRA-1234) clean. Filed as vuln-0001.

entries.risk_area: Prompt injection via untrusted task content reaching the reasoning prompt
entries.evidence: No untrusted source reaches `task` in this commit (only sys.argv[1]); prompt injection requires ticket content to be forwarded, which the repo does not do. Noted in vuln-0001 remediation as a forward-looking hardening item, not a present defect.

The only input source is the operator typing at the `agentcore$` prompt; per engagement rules, intended execution of commands supplied by an authorized shell user is not a vulnerability. The double-quote-framing is a reliability bug (commands containing `"` are misparsed), not a trust-boundary violation — no untrusted party can reach this input path in the shipped code.

entries.risk_area: Incorrect boto3 API usage (body passed as dict vs blob/bytes) and unvalidated runtime response handling
entries.evidence: Verified against the bundled botocore service model (offline, no AWS call): `InvokeAgentRuntimeCommand.body` is a structure with members {command, timeout} and is required — the dict passed in shell_client.py:49-55 is the correct shape. `InvokeAgentRuntime.payload` is a blob and is passed json.dumps().encode(), also correct. Response parsing iterates documented chunk events only; no eval/exec/format sinks on runtime data.

config.py contains only a runtime ARN, region, and a UUID session id — an identifier, not a credential (no access key, secret, or token). Per engagement rules, ARNs/account IDs are not reported as credentials. Hygiene note only: identifiers embedded in VCS should ideally come from config, which the env-var override already permits.

entries.risk_area: Command construction / injection in fixed demo commands
entries.evidence: All six commands are static string literals with no interpolation of variable data; nothing user- or network-controlled reaches shell.run(). The temporary file writes go to /tmp/demo.txt with fixed content. No trust boundary crossed.

Docs accurately describe behavior; one reliability note (not a security issue): README documents file_transfer.py which does not exist in the repo at this commit. No secrets or unsafe instructions in docs.

Single dependency `boto3>=1.35.0` with a floor (not a pin); no lockfile present, so no exact version to assess. No known-CVE reporting possible or warranted for a floating floor on a maintained library.
